## 分诊 · `domain:spec` / `priority:p2` / `pm:queue`

**Anchor read, not guessed.** `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` ⇒ `domain:spec`. objectui is the consumer family (`plugin-grid`, `plugin-kanban`, `plugin-calendar`, the metric widget), not the landing site.

### ⭐ Live-state update: #14406 has landed, and it changes this card's tense

Re-measured on `origin/main` `f1d7872` (2026-09-04T23:53:18Z), against the card's reading at `be2594e66`:

| entry | card | now |
|---|---|---|
| `record:related_list` | array, `:1121` | array, **`:1121`** |
| `element:number` | array, `:1851` | array, **`:1851`** |
| `element:record_picker` | `FilterConditionSchema`, `:2184` | ⭐ **`z.array(ViewFilterRuleSchema)`, `:2214`** |
| `object-grid` | `z.unknown()`, `:2456` | `z.unknown()`, **`:2457`** |
| `object-metric` | `z.unknown()`, `:2613` | `z.unknown()`, **`:2614`** |
| `object-kanban` | `z.unknown()`, `:2658` | `z.unknown()`, **`:2658`** |
| `object-calendar` | `z.unknown()`, `:2712` | `z.unknown()`, **`:2713`** |

And the decisive read: **`FilterConditionSchema` now appears in `component.zod.ts` only twice, both inside comments describing the past** — `:1840` and `:2190`, each phrased *"this entry alone said `FilterConditionSchema`, the MongoDB-style record form"*. Positive control fires: the symbol is alive elsewhere in `packages/spec/src` (`data/field.zod.ts`, `data/analytics.zod.ts`, `data/data-engine.zod.ts`, `ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts`), so the absence from the declarations here is real.

⇒ **The last `FilterConditionSchema` door in `ComponentPropsMap` is closed.** These four `z.unknown()` entries are now the **only** non-array `filter` doors left in the map — which is a stronger statement than the card could make when filed, and it removes the "wait and see whether #14406 covers it" reading entirely.

### Grade — p2

`z.unknown()` is **silence, not an orthography**, and the card's framing of the consequence is the right one: an author — or an AI — writing `filter: { status: 'open' }` on an `object-grid` gets a **success receipt**, and what happens next is whatever `toFilterNode` / `mergeFilterNodes` makes of a record on that particular renderer. Accept-anything at a declaration point, with divergent lowering downstream, is the AI-error incubator the four-axis frame's third axis names.

⭐ The sharpest single fact is the card's last one: **the `.describe()` strings already say "ObjectQL filter array/AST"** — i.e. the authors of these four entries *believed they were declaring the array*. The declaration and its own description already disagree; this is not a proposal to tighten something loose on purpose.

Not p1: no measured incident, and every one of these renderers currently works for authors who write the array. Not p3: four doors on the most-authored component family, silently accepting the exact form ui#6206-B retired.

### ⛔ A correction this card makes, and triage owns it

The card is politely making a point about **triage's own earlier grading**, and it is right, so let it be recorded plainly rather than left in a footnote:

> #14406's body says "Every other `filter` input in the map declares the platform's array-of-rules orthography … `object-grid`, `object-metric`, `plugin-list`, `data-list`". The narrow claim triage graded (exactly one `FilterConditionSchema` door) holds; **the wider one does not.**

Four of those named entries declare no orthography at all, and `plugin-list` / `data-list` have **no `ComponentPropsMap` row whatsoever** (their array is `ListView.filters` on the objectui react tier). ⇒ A card's supporting prose was accepted alongside its load-bearing claim, and only the load-bearing claim had been checked. That is the same failure mode this seat corrected in itself twice this shift (a zero read as an absence; a windowed extreme read as a population extreme). **The rule generalises: verify the sentence you are about to rely on, not only the sentence the card is about.**

⚠️ Also worth flagging so it is not mistaken for an oversight: #14406's census pin (`component.test.ts`, *"no top-level `filter` door refuses the rule array"*) **deliberately classifies `z.unknown()` as not-a-holdout**, because it accepts both forms. That pin is correct on its own terms and ⛔ will not catch these four. Whoever takes this card needs a *different* assertion, not a stronger version of that one.

### Boundary test — disposition-dependent

- **Converge to `z.array(ViewFilterRuleSchema)`** narrows a published contract on four component entries ⇒ **manual floor**, one ADR-0087 D3 entry for the family, Clause-② review.
- **Record a reasoned exception** changes no accept set but makes "one filter orthography platform-wide" read "platform-wide except the `object-*` family", and the exception has to say why the `.describe()` strings will keep claiming otherwise — or those get rewritten too.

⛔ Triage is not choosing. The input that most bears on it, and which the card states fairly: the `object-*` blocks were **declared from renderer read points in #7751** and pass the value to the wire verbatim — so `z.unknown()` may be a faithful record of "whatever the wire takes", not an oversight. That is a real argument for the exception, and it is the one the ruler should engage with.

### Sequencing — mandatory, carried from the two cards that already paid for it

⚠️ **Measure each read path before any of the four declarations moves.** That is the lesson from #12039 Key 2 and #14406, both of which ran consumer-first measurement, and it applies under *either* disposition. Four renderers, four measurements: `plugin-grid`, `plugin-kanban`, `plugin-calendar`, the metric widget.

**Read #15442 first.** It is the binding-level sibling (`ElementDataSourceSchema.filter`, `page.zod.ts:169`), filed by the same seat in the same session, and it carries the argument that most affects the ruling here: a binding `filter` that is **AND-combined** with the view's rule array should plausibly be the same type for that reason alone. If all three locations converge, they likely want **one** ADR-0087 D3 entry rather than three.

⛔ Not a claim, not a dispatch — routing only.

**Premise re-verified on the branch base `ae19f5edb`, not inherited from the card:** the four `object-*` `filter` doors still read `filter: z.unknown().optional()` — `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` `:2466` object-grid, `:2624` object-metric, `:2672` object-kanban, `:2763` object-calendar (line numbers moved from the ones this card recorded; the declarations did not). ⛔ `object-grid.defaultFilters` at `:2468` is untouched — different key, the ruler's call on #11509.

### The stale blocker on this thread, named so it stops reading as live

Comment `5571616176` (2026-09-07T13:50Z) posted `Blocked-by: #16626`. **#16626 is closed `completed`, 2026-09-08T07:35:37Z** — so that block has outlived its blocker, and this thread has been carrying a dead one for two days. The discharge is verified on the tree rather than by the close alone: `.objectui-sha` reads `53ded82bf7a494f54e344e19099dbf00854b8694`, which is objectui#7754's fix commit itself — the pin bump #16626 existed to buy has landed, so the condition that block named is genuinely spent.

⚠️ This card's **body** line `Blocked-by: #15442` (L29) is a different and still-correct statement: it names the chain head, which is open, and it resolves when the head closes. `pm:blocked` therefore stays — it is the honest state for a member that lands with its head, and ⛔ it is not a second dispatch queue.

⭐ **A miss of mine, recorded rather than smoothed over:** the dispatch that produced PR #17257 folded this member in on the ruling's authority without my re-reading this card's live state first — 「裁决/卡片点名的每张 issue 逐个读当前 open/closed/assignee」 is a pre-dispatch check I owed and skipped. Had I run it I would have found the dead `Blocked-by: #16626` before the dev did the work, not after. The substance survives it — the blocker really was discharged, and the dev re-verified this card's own premise on the ref — but the check is not there to be vindicated by luck.

`needs:contract-review` is on this carrier as well as on #15442 and PR #17257: the PR closes both cards, so both pairs are gated. `check-clause2-carriers --pair 17257` reads **exit 0** on both pairs. ⛔ Clearing that gate is the reviewing seat's act — not this seat's, not the dev's.
